description: Design a DVFS controller that adjusts the voltage and frequency of a processing unit based on the input performance requirement. The module should have a clock input, an enable signal, and a performance level input. The output should be the selected voltage and frequency levels. The performance level input will be a 2-bit value where '00' corresponds to the lowest performance (lowest voltage and frequency), '01' to medium performance, '10' to high performance, and '11' to maximum performance. The voltage and frequency levels can be represented by 2-bit and 3-bit values, respectively.
code:
module DVFS_Controller (
    input clk,
    input enable,
    input [1:0] performance_level,
    output reg [1:0] voltage,   // 2-bit voltage level
    output reg [2:0] frequency   // 3-bit frequency level
);
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (enable) begin
            case (performance_level)
                2'b00: begin
                    voltage <= 2'b00;  // Lowest Voltage
                    frequency <= 3'b000; // Lowest Frequency
                end
                2'b01: begin
                    voltage <= 2'b01;  // Medium Voltage
                    frequency <= 3'b001; // Medium Frequency
                end
                2'b10: begin
                    voltage <= 2'b10;  // High Voltage
                    frequency <= 3'b010; // High Frequency
                end
                2'b11: begin
                    voltage <= 2'b11;  // Maximum Voltage
                    frequency <= 3'b011; // Maximum Frequency
                end
                default: begin
                    voltage <= 2'b00;  // Default to Lowest
                    frequency <= 3'b000; // Default to Lowest
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an SR flip-flop using Verilog. The SR flip-flop should have two inputs, S (set) and R (reset), and two outputs, Q and Qn (not Q). The behavior should be such that:
- When S = 1 and R = 0, Q should be set to 1.
- When S = 0 and R = 1, Q should be reset to 0.
- When S = 0 and R = 0, Q should hold its previous state.
- When S = 1 and R = 1, the state is considered invalid (you can choose to hold the previous state or set Q to 0).
code:
module sr_flip_flop (
    input wire S,
    input wire R,
    output reg Q,
    output wire Qn
);
    assign Qn = ~Q;

    always @(posedge S or posedge R) begin
        if (R) begin
            Q <= 0; // Reset state
        end else if (S) begin
            Q <= 1; // Set state
        end
        // Hold state implicitly if both S and R are low
    end
endmodule

Design a Verilog module that performs bilinear interpolation for a 2x2 pixel grid. The module will take four pixel values (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), and the fractional coordinates (x, y) representing the position within that grid. The output should be the interpolated pixel value.
code:
module bilinear_interpolation (
    input [7:0] p00, // top-left pixel
    input [7:0] p01, // top-right pixel
    input [7:0] p10, // bottom-left pixel
    input [7:0] p11, // bottom-right pixel
    input [7:0] x,   // fractional x coordinate (0-255)
    input [7:0] y,   // fractional y coordinate (0-255)
    output reg [7:0] pixel_out
);
    reg [15:0] p0, p1, p2, p3; // intermediate calculations
    reg [15:0] temp1, temp2;

    always @(*) begin
        p0 = p00 * (256 - x) + p01 * x; // interpolate top row
        p1 = p10 * (256 - x) + p11 * x; // interpolate bottom row
        
        temp1 = p0 * (256 - y);
        temp2 = p1 * y;

        pixel_out = (temp1 + temp2) >> 16; // final interpolation
    end
endmodule

Design a cache replacement policy module that can operate in either LRU (Least Recently Used) or FIFO (First In First Out) mode. The module should take inputs for cache access (address), a control signal to choose the replacement policy, and produce the index of the cache line to be replaced. The cache has 4 lines, indexed from 0 to 3, which can be implemented using a 2-bit index. The LRU mode must track the usage of each line, while the FIFO mode must replace the oldest line.
code:
module CacheReplacement(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] addr, // Cache address
    input wire policy, // 0 for FIFO, 1 for LRU
    output reg [1:0] replace_index // Index of cache line to replace
);
    reg [1:0] fifo_counter; // For FIFO replacement
    reg [3:0] lru_counter [3:0]; // For LRU replacement
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            replace_index <= 2'b00;
            fifo_counter <= 2'b00;
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                lru_counter[i] <= 4'b0;
            end
        end else begin
            if (policy) begin // LRU
                replace_index <= 0;
                for (i = 1; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru_counter[i] < lru_counter[replace_index]) begin
                        replace_index <= i;
                    end
                end
                lru_counter[replace_index] <= addr; // Update the LRU counter
                for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    lru_counter[i] <= lru_counter[i] + 1; // Increment usage
                end
                lru_counter[replace_index] <= 0; // Reset the used line
            end else begin // FIFO
                replace_index <= fifo_counter; // Replace the next line in FIFO order
                fifo_counter <= fifo_counter + 1; // Increment FIFO counter
                if (fifo_counter == 3) begin
                    fifo_counter <= 0; // Wrap around
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: A watchdog timer that resets itself if not periodically kicked. The timer should have a configurable timeout period and can be reset using an input signal. If the timer reaches the timeout without being reset, it will output a reset signal.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire kick,
    input wire [3:0] timeout,
    output reg reset_signal
);
    reg [3:0] count;

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            count <= 4'b0;
            reset_signal <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (kick) begin
                count <= 4'b0; // Reset the count when kicked
                reset_signal <= 1'b0; // No reset signal
            end else if (count >= timeout) begin
                reset_signal <= 1'b1; // Assert reset signal when timeout
            end else begin
                count <= count + 1; // Increment count
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple memory allocator in Verilog that can allocate and free a fixed size memory block. The allocator should support a fixed maximum number of blocks (e.g., 4 blocks) and have inputs for allocation and deallocation requests. The allocator should output the status of each block (allocated or free) after every operation.
code:
module MemoryAllocator (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire alloc,          // Request to allocate memory
    input wire free,          // Request to free memory
    input wire [1:0] block_id,// Block ID (0 to 3)
    output reg [3:0] status   // Status of each memory block (4 bits)
);

    reg [3:0] memory; // 4 memory blocks, 0 = free, 1 = allocated

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            memory <= 4'b0000; // All blocks free on reset
            status <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            if (alloc && (memory[block_id] == 1'b0)) begin
                memory[block_id] <= 1'b1; // Allocate memory
            end
            if (free && (memory[block_id] == 1'b1)) begin
                memory[block_id] <= 1'b0; // Free memory
            end
            status <= memory; // Output status
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that calculates the Internet Protocol (IP) checksum for a given 16-bit words input. The module should take a 16-bit input word and accumulate the sum of these words, performing one’s complement addition. If the sum exceeds 16 bits, the overflow should be wrapped around. The output should be the resulting checksum after processing all input words.
code:
module ip_checksum (
    input [15:0] data_in,
    input valid,
    input clk,
    input rst,
    output reg [15:0] checksum
);
    reg [15:0] sum;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            sum <= 16'b0;
            checksum <= 16'b0;
        end else if (valid) begin
            sum <= sum + data_in;
            if (sum[16]) begin // Check for overflow
                sum <= sum + 1; // Wrap around
            end
        end else begin
            checksum <= ~sum; // One's complement
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a simple branch predictor using a 2-bit saturating counter for a given address. The counter should predict whether a branch will be taken (1) or not taken (0). Based on the previous outcomes, the counter should be updated accordingly. The state transitions for the 2-bit counter are as follows:
- 00: Strongly not taken
- 01: Weakly not taken
- 10: Weakly taken
- 11: Strongly taken

The input will consist of branch outcomes (1 for taken, 0 for not taken) and the output should show the predicted outcomes based on the current state of the counter.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_outcome,
    output reg prediction
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Start in strongly not taken state
            prediction <= 0;
        end else begin
            prediction <= state[1]; // Output the prediction (11 -> 1, else 0)
            case (state)
                2'b00: if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b01; // Not Taken -> Weakly Not Taken
                2'b01: if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // Weakly Not Taken -> Weakly Taken
                        else state <= 2'b00; // Weakly Not Taken -> Strongly Not Taken
                2'b10: if (branch_outcome) state <= 2'b11; // Weakly Taken -> Strongly Taken
                        else state <= 2'b01; // Weakly Taken -> Weakly Not Taken
                2'b11: if (~branch_outcome) state <= 2'b10; // Strongly Taken -> Weakly Taken
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire [7:0] dest_addr,

description: Design a 16-bit CRC generator that takes a 16-bit input data and a 16-bit polynomial as inputs, and produces a 16-bit CRC checksum. The CRC calculation must be implemented as a sequential circuit that takes the input data and polynomial, processes it through a series of clock cycles, and outputs the final CRC value. Ensure to include proper reset functionality to initialize the CRC computation.
code:
module crc16_generator (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    input wire [15:0] polynomial,
    output reg [15:0] crc_out
);
    reg [15:0] crc;
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc <= 16'h0000; // Initialize CRC to 0
        end else begin
            crc <= crc ^ data_in; // Step 1: XOR input data with CRC
            for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                if (crc[15] == 1'b1) begin
                    crc <= (crc << 1) ^ polynomial; // Shift left and XOR with polynomial
                end else begin
                    crc <= crc << 1; // Just shift left
                end
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        crc_out <= crc; // Output the CRC result
    end
endmodule

    input wire reset,        // Active high reset
    input wire [7:0] data_in,// 8-bit data to send
    input wire start,        // Signal to start transmission
    output reg mosi,         // Master Out Slave In
    output reg sck,          // Serial Clock
    output reg done          // Transmission done signal
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count;      // To count the bits sent
    reg [7:0] data_reg;       // Register to hold data

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            mosi <= 0;
            sck <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            data_reg <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (start && bit_count == 0) begin
                data_reg <= data_in; // Load data to register on start
                done <= 0; // Not done yet
            end

                // Generate clock and output data
                sck <= ~sck; // Toggle clock
                if (sck) begin
                    mosi <= data_reg[7-bit_count]; // Send MSB first
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Count the bits
                end
            end else begin
                done <= 1; // Mark transmission as done
                bit_count <= 0; // Reset count for next transmission
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module booth_multiplier #(parameter N = 4) (
    input wire [N-1:0] A,
    input wire [N-1:0] B,
    output reg [2*N-1:0] P
);
    reg [N-1:0] M, Q;
    reg Q_1;
    reg [N:0] A_ext, P_temp;
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        M = A;          // Multiplicand
        Q = B;          // Multiplier
        Q_1 = 1'b0;    // Previous Q bit
        A_ext = {1'b0, M}; // Extend A to N+1 bits
        P_temp = {N+1{1'b0}}; // Initialize product to 0
        P_temp[N:0] = {Q, Q_1}; // Combine Q and Q-1
        
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
            case ({Q[0], Q_1})
                2'b01: P_temp = P_temp + A_ext; // Add M
                2'b10: P_temp = P_temp - A_ext; // Subtract M
                default: P_temp = P_temp; // Do nothing
            endcase
            Q_1 = Q[0]; // Update previous Q bit
            Q = {P_temp[N], Q[N-1:1]}; // Shift right
            P_temp[N] = P_temp[N-1]; // Maintain sign bit
        end
        
        P = P_temp[N:1]; // Final product
    end
endmodule

The CSPRNG should take a seed value at initialization and generate a pseudo-random bit stream. The output should be a single bit that is generated on every clock cycle.
code:
module CSPRNG (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] seed,
    output reg random_bit
);

reg [7:0] lfsr;

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        lfsr <= seed; // Initialize LFSR with seed
        random_bit <= 0;
    end else begin
        // LFSR feedback polynomial: x^8 + x^6 + x^5 + x^4 + 1
        random_bit <= lfsr[0]; // Output current bit
        lfsr <= {lfsr[6:0], lfsr[7] ^ lfsr[5] ^ lfsr[4] ^ lfsr[0]}; // Shift and feedback
    end
end

endmodule

module booth_multiplier (
    input [3:0] A, // Multiplicand
    input [3:0] B, // Multiplier
    output reg [7:0] P // Product
);
    reg [7:0] A_ext, B_ext;
    reg [3:0] Q;
    reg Q_1;
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        // Initialize variables
        A_ext = {4'b0000, A}; // Extend A to 8 bits
        B_ext = {4'b0000, B}; // Extend B to 8 bits
        Q = B;                // Load multiplier
        P = 8'b00000000;     // Initialize product to 0
        Q_1 = 1'b0;          // Initialize Q-1

        for(i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            case({Q[0], Q_1})
                2'b01: P = P + A_ext;          // Add A
                2'b10: P = P - A_ext;          // Subtract A
            endcase
            // Arithmetic right shift
            {P, Q} = {P[7], P[7:1], Q[3]}; // Shift operation
            Q_1 = Q[0];                    // Update Q-1
        end
    end
endmodule

    input load,
    input [7:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);

description: Design an SPI master controller that initiates communication with an SPI slave device. The master should transmit data on a rising clock edge and receive data on a falling clock edge. The master should also handle a chip select signal to enable communication with the slave.

module spi_master (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sclk,
    output reg mosi,
    input wire miso,
    output reg cs,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg done
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            sclk <= 0;
            mosi <= 0;
            cs <= 1;
            bit_count <= 0;
            done <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (start) begin
                cs <= 0;                // Activate chip select
                shift_reg <= data_in;   // Load data to shift register
                bit_count <= 8;         // Start with 8 bits
                done <= 0;              // Reset done flag
            end else if (bit_count > 0) begin
                sclk <= ~sclk;          // Toggle clock
                if (sclk) begin
                    mosi <= shift_reg[7];  // Send MSB first
                    shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], miso}; // Shift in received bit
                    bit_count <= bit_count - 1; // Decrement bit count
                end
            end else if (bit_count == 0) begin
                cs <= 1;                // Deactivate chip select
                data_out <= shift_reg;  // Store received data
                done <= 1;              // Set done flag
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    output reg serial_out,

            bit_index <= 0;
            serial_out <= 0;
            ready <= 1;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (bit_index < 32) begin
                serial_out <= data_in[31 - bit_index];
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                ready <= (bit_index < 31); // not ready after last bit

module round_robin_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);
    reg [1:0] current_priority;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;
            current_priority <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;  // Reset grant
            if (req != 4'b0000) begin
                // Round Robin logic
                case (current_priority)
                    2'b00: if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b01; end
                           else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b10; end
                           else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b11; end
                           else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b00; end
                    2'b01: if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b10; end
                           else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b11; end
                           else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b00; end
                           else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b01; end
                    2'b10: if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b11; end
                           else if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b00; end
                           else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b01; end
                           else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b10; end
                    2'b11: if (req[3]) begin grant[3] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b00; end
                           else if (req[0]) begin grant[0] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b01; end
                           else if (req[1]) begin grant[1] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b10; end
                           else if (req[2]) begin grant[2] <= 1; current_priority <= 2'b11; end
                endcase
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    output reg out
);

        if (rst) begin
            count <= 0;
            out <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (count == freq_div) begin

description: Design a Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) in Verilog that takes an input clock signal and generates an output clock signal that is a phase-locked version of the input. The PLL should have a configurable divide factor to set the output frequency. The phase comparator should sample the input clock on the rising edge and adjust the output clock accordingly. Implement a simple state machine to toggle the output clock based on the phase comparison result. The design should have at least three states: LOCKED, UNLOCKED, and ADJUSTING.
code:
module pll (
    input wire clk_in,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [3:0] divide_factor,
    output reg clk_out
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 2-bit state for LOCKED, UNLOCKED, ADJUSTING
    parameter LOCKED = 2'b00, UNLOCKED = 2'b01, ADJUSTING = 2'b10;
    reg [3:0] counter; // Counter for clock division
    reg clk_enable; // Enable signal for clk_out

    always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= UNLOCKED;
            counter <= 0;
            clk_out <= 0;
            clk_enable <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                UNLOCKED: begin
                    // Trying to lock the phase
                    counter <= 0;
                    clk_enable <= 1; // Enable output clock generation
                    state <= ADJUSTING;
                end
                ADJUSTING: begin
                    counter <= counter + 1;
                    if (counter == divide_factor) begin
                        clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock
                        counter <= 0; // Reset counter
                        state <= LOCKED; // Move to LOCKED state
                    end
                end
                LOCKED: begin
                    // Maintain locked state
                    counter <= counter + 1;
                    if (counter == divide_factor) begin
                        clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle output clock
                        counter <= 0; // Reset counter
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

This problem requires the design of a simple PCIe request handling system. The system needs to capture a request signal, maintain the state of the request, and generate a corresponding acknowledgment signal after a certain delay. It should also allow for reset functionality. Implement a module that takes a request signal (`req`), generates an acknowledgment signal (`ack`), and includes a reset signal (`rst`). The acknowledgment signal should be active one clock cycle after the request signal is detected.

module pcie_request_handler (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire req,
    output reg ack
);
    reg req_d;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            ack <= 0;
            req_d <= 0;
        end else begin
            req_d <= req; // delay the request signal
            ack <= req && !req_d; // generate ack on the rising edge of req
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a PCIe endpoint interface state machine that can handle basic transaction types. The state machine should have the following states: IDLE, REQUEST, RESPONSE. The state transitions occur based on input signals indicating whether a request is sent or a response is received. The state machine should also output the current state as a 2-bit signal. The inputs are 'req' for request and 'rsp' for response, and both are active high signals.
code:
module pcie_sm (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input req,
    input rsp,
    output reg [1:0] state
);

    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE = 2'b00;
    localparam REQUEST = 2'b01;
    localparam RESPONSE = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (req) begin
                        state <= REQUEST;
                    end
                end
                REQUEST: begin
                    if (rsp) begin
                        state <= RESPONSE;
                    end
                end
                RESPONSE: begin
                    if (req) begin
                        state <= REQUEST;
                    end else begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Implement a 2D bilinear interpolation module in Verilog. The module takes four pixel values (P11, P12, P21, P22) corresponding to the corners of a rectangle and two fractional coordinates (x, y) as inputs. It outputs the interpolated pixel value based on these inputs.

module bilinear_interpolation(
    input [7:0] P11, // Pixel value at (0,0)
    input [7:0] P12, // Pixel value at (0,1)
    input [7:0] P21, // Pixel value at (1,0)
    input [7:0] P22, // Pixel value at (1,1)
    input [7:0] x,   // Fractional x coordinate (0-255)
    input [7:0] y,   // Fractional y coordinate (0-255)
    output reg [7:0] P_out // Interpolated pixel value
);

    always @(*) begin
        // Bilinear interpolation formula
        P_out = (P11 * (256 - x) * (256 - y) + 
                 P12 * (256 - x) * y + 
                 P21 * x * (256 - y) + 
                 P22 * x * y) >> 16; // Dividing by 256*256
    end
endmodule

);

    end

Design a 4-bit Up/Down counter with the following specifications:

- The counter should reset to 0 when the reset signal is high.
- The counter should wrap around when it exceeds its maximum value (15) or goes below its minimum value (0).
- The counter should have a clock signal for synchronization.
- The output should be a 4-bit value representing the current count.

module up_down_counter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire up,
    input wire down,
    output reg [3:0] count
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 4'b0000; // Reset counter to 0
        end else if (up && !down) begin
            count <= (count == 4'b1111) ? 4'b0000 : count + 1; // Increment with wrap-around
        end else if (down && !up) begin
            count <= (count == 4'b0000) ? 4'b1111 : count - 1; // Decrement with wrap-around
        end
    end
endmodule

    input [3:0] opcode,
    output reg [15:0] result,
    output reg zero_flag
);

    end
endmodule

The output grant should remain valid until the next clock cycle, even if the request is deactivated.

module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire [3:0] req,     // Request inputs
    output reg [3:0] grant    // Grant outputs
);
    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;  // Reset grant outputs
        end else begin
            grant <= 4'b0000;  // Default grant to none
            if (req[0]) grant <= 4'b0001; // Grant to request 0
            else if (req[1]) grant <= 4'b0010; // Grant to request 1
            else if (req[2]) grant <= 4'b0100; // Grant to request 2
            else if (req[3]) grant <= 4'b1000; // Grant to request 3
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a JK flip-flop in Verilog. The JK flip-flop should have inputs J, K, and a clock signal CLK. It should also have an output Q that represents the current state of the flip-flop. The flip-flop should toggle its output Q based on the values of J and K at the rising edge of the clock. If both J and K are high, the flip-flop should toggle. If J is high and K is low, the output should be set high. If J is low and K is high, the output should be set low. If both J and K are low, the output should remain unchanged.
code:
module jk_flip_flop (
    input J,
    input K,
    input CLK,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge CLK) begin
        if (J && K) begin
            Q <= ~Q; // Toggle
        end else if (J && ~K) begin
            Q <= 1; // Set high
        end else if (~J && K) begin
            Q <= 0; // Set low
        end // If both J and K are low, do nothing
    end
endmodule
